MagicDraw_Profile:RelationMap.descriptionArea:
The Requirement Derivation Map allows rapid review, analysis and creation of relations among the requirements and their derived requirements.

 

 

To create Requirement Derivation Map:

  1. Drag a Requirement from the Model Browser to the Requirement Derivation Map.
  2. Specify Scope.

Requirement Derivation Map can display the model structure in two different layouts: tree or radial. The relations represented on the map can be analyzed in one of the following ways:

 

 

- Dynamically - according to the applied filters: element type, dependencies criterion, depth, and scope.

- Statically - step-by-step expanding the branches of the structure. To represent the same element as a single node in the map, click the Options button on the toolbar and select the Show Single Node Per Element command.

 

 


Manipulations:

 

Create a relation map structure - drag an element from the Model Browser to the relation map.

Create new element of the same type - type element name and press Ctrl+Enter.

Restore manually suppressed / expanded branches and hidden elements and they position - click the Refresh button .

Expand / suppress branches - click  /  near the node.   

Move the whole structure - click an empty place on the Relation Map and drag.

Move the selected node - click the node and drag.

Zoom in - hold down Ctrl while scrolling up.

Zoom out - hold down Ctrl while scrolling down.

Fit in window - press Ctrl+W.

Zoom 1:1 - press Ctrl+NumPad /.

Turn on the ability to change the context element with single click - click the Options button on the toolbar and then select the Make Element as Context on Selection command.

 

Filters:

Context - the core element of the structure.

Scope - fragment of the model (or the whole model) from which the relation map is built.

Depth - level of branches automatically expanded starting from the context element.

Leidos_Profile:SRD_RQMT.Text: 50 meter resolution
SYSTEM CAPABILITIES
1 km geolocation accuracy
The system shall generate an alarm message whenever a detection fire persists for more than 20 minutes
Interpreted data to end user within 5 minutes
The delay between transmission of commands from the ground station to receipt by the satellite shall be no greater than 5 seconds.
The delay between transmission of a compressed frame of imagery from the satellite to its receipt by the ground station shall be no greater than 15 seconds.
DATA HANDLING
The sensor shall sense thermal emissions with a sensitivity less than 150W (TBD), and a resolution of less than 3 miliiradians.
Up to 500 fire-monitoring offices + 2,000 rangers worldwide (max of 100 simultaneous users
95% excluding weather. 24 hour maximum downtime
8 years

The delay between transmission of an alert message, including the location of the epicenter of the reported fire, from the satellite to its receipt by the ground station shall be no greater than 5 seconds.
The delay between receipt of imagery by the ground station and its relay to and receipt by the Ops Center shall be no greater than 5 seconds.
LIFETIME & AVAILABILITY
The satellite shall have the ability to send imagery and other data to the ground autonomously when triggered by detection of a forest fire, and on command by the Ops Center.
DETECTION & ALERTING
The system shall maintain an archive of IR video imagery collected during all events lasting more than 20 minutes.
Identify an emerging forest fire within 8 hours with less than 10% false positives
Coverage of specified forest areas within the US at least twice daily.
See Diagram
Location amd extent in lat/long for local plotting. avg temp for each 40 m2
Work through light clouds
Interoperable through NOAA ground stations
Ops Center personnel shall be able to issue commands to the satellite to point the sensor to a chosen location on the earth's surface.
Natural environment only. not in radiation belts.
The system shall include an application that presents imagery to firefighters on mobile devices operated by them during their fire fighting activities

The Ops Center shall have the ability to determine the forest service locations in proximity to the detected forest fire, and to forward imagery and alerts to those locations autonomously within 10 seconds of its receipt.
